body: Transportation Security Administration (TSA) officers at Ontario International Airport (ONT) found two live snakes concealed in a passenger's checked luggage during a routine baggage inspection earlier this month. The reptiles were hidden inside a pillowcase, and the discovery was made when TSA Officer Benjamin Andrade-Carillo noticed something unusual in the suitcase. The X-ray image had initially suggested the bag contained what appeared to be a bundle of ropes, but closer inspection revealed the pillowcase with the live snakes, and the officer immediately alerted his supervisor when he realized the object he was handling was moving.

One of the snakes was identified as a rattlesnake, and officers initially could not determine whether the animals were venomous, so they avoided unnecessary handling and took additional precautions. Screening in the immediate area was temporarily suspended while officers assessed the potential danger, and Supervisory TSA Officer Suggey Flores and Ontario International Airport TSA Manager Francisco "Frank" Calderon were notified as the inspection continued.

Airport police subsequently took possession of the suitcase and escorted it to the airline ticketing area, where the passenger removed the snakes and handed them to a family member who was not traveling. Officers then rescreened the checked bag and cleared it for travel, and the passenger was permitted to continue the journey without the animals. According to the TSA report, the traveler described the snakes as his pets and said he had previously traveled with them on another airline. The incident ended without injuries, significant operational disruption, or a missed flight.
en.summary: Transportation Security Administration officers at Ontario International Airport found two live snakes hidden in a pillowcase inside a passenger's checked bag, including a venomous rattlesnake; no one was injured and the passenger continued the journey without the animals.
en.title: TSA finds two live snakes, including a rattlesnake, in checked bag at Ontario airport

body: 美國運輸安全管理局（TSA）人員本月稍早在安大略國際機場（ONT）例行檢查託運行李時，查獲藏在枕頭套裡的兩條活蛇。X光影像起初看似一捆繩索，檢查人員察覺異狀後進一步檢查，發現枕頭套裡是活蛇，察覺手中物品在移動後立即通報主管。
其中一條蛇被確認為響尾蛇。檢查人員起初無法判斷這些蛇是否有毒，因此避免不必要的接觸並採取額外防護，同時暫停附近區域的安檢作業以評估危險；主管與機場TSA經理接獲通報後到場協助檢查。
機場警方隨後接管這件行李並護送至航空公司售票區，旅客取出活蛇、交給一名未同行的家人。行李重新安檢後獲准託運，旅客也在未攜帶活蛇的情況下繼續行程。據TSA通報，這名旅客稱這些蛇是他的寵物，並表示先前曾帶著牠們搭乘另一家航空公司的航班。這起事件無人受傷，也未造成明顯營運中斷或旅客誤機。
